claims: A box-jump identity must specify start condition, countermovement permission, arm use, takeoff and landing laterality, approach, platform relationship, stabilization, exit, and reset behavior.
{{canonicalName}} must not combine a floor-to-box jump with a depth or drop jump, repeated rebound, box jump-over, unilateral landing, seated start, approach jump, or loaded jump.
A reset box jump is a discrete ballistic propulsion task followed by an elevated landing and deliberate stabilization; repeated reactive box contacts are a different task.
{{canonicalName}} belongs to bilateral vertical power and landing control, with start condition, arm use, box height, landing strategy, and reset intent encoded as controlled dimensions.
Propulsion and elevated landing are coordinated across the foot, ankle, knee, hip, pelvis, trunk, and, when permitted, the shoulder girdle.

The card should assign propulsion to the plantar flexors, quadriceps, and hip extensors; stabilization to the foot, hip, and trunk stabilizers; and arm-swing contribution to coordinated shoulder flexion without claiming one isolated prime mover.
In recreationally active adults asked to jump maximally, changing box height across the studied range generally did not change most propulsive performance variables.

Box height is therefore a landing target and constraint, not a valid stand-alone measure of vertical jump height; observable quality includes maximal intent when prescribed, full-foot clearance, quiet simultaneous contact, controlled landing depth, and a stable finish.

Box-jump difficulty changes with required impulse, box collision consequence, landing-space tolerance, start condition, arm restriction, laterality, approach, external load, repetition strategy, and fatigue.

Exercise cards must score technical complexity, physical or absolute-load demand, coordination, supervision, failure consequence, impact, work-capacity demand, and overall difficulty directly; they must not use skill-library levels.
Jump volume is counted as discrete takeoffs and landings, while height, intent, start condition, arm use, body mass, external load, and reset duration govern exposure.

{{canonicalName}} needs contact count, output intent, impact and eccentric stress, technical-fatigue criteria, and recovery guidance; a reset power prescription must not be converted into a conditioning interval.
Different box heights can be used without assuming that a higher box produces a better propulsive effort, provided the athlete can clear and land on the platform safely.

The delivery profile should require a stable non-slip platform, unobstructed takeoff and top surfaces, adequate ceiling and forward clearance, a safe step-down route, athlete-specific height selection, and coach sightlines to the feet and landing.
Power-focused plyometrics use low-repetition sets, deliberate resets, and enough recovery to preserve takeoff output and landing quality.
Prescribe sets, discrete repetitions, box-height selection rule, landing hold, step-down behavior, rest, and stop criteria; do not prescribe maximal box height as the training target.
Specific external or movement-focused feedback can improve landing mechanics, while excessive cue volume can impair learning.
Use a small cue set: choose an honest box, load and drive, clear the front edge, land quietly with the whole foot, own the top, stand, step down, and reset.
Box-jump hazards include collision with the front edge, missed or partial foot contact, unstable or shifting equipment, uncontrolled landing, and an unsafe jump-down exit.

Stop for pain, giving way, hesitation, repeated toe catch, partial-foot landing, excessive hip tuck used to chase box height, loud or asymmetrical contact, valgus or trunk collapse, loss of output, or any platform movement.
Box height should be selected to support the intended landing or teaching goal rather than used as a proxy for jump performance.

{{canonicalName}} belongs early in an output block after readiness work, or in movement intelligence when explicitly submaximal and technique-focused; low volume and full reset preserve the intended stimulus.
Athlete support should show the prescribed start, target box, landing shape, hold, stand, step-down route, and one primary cue.
The interface should explain that a higher box can reward extra hip flexion without proving a higher jump and should display a lower-box or non-box regression without shame language.
Coaches can change box height for teaching and landing purposes without treating box height as the propulsive outcome.

Coach support should provide side and front observation, edge-clearance and full-foot criteria, landing-depth comparison, collision-risk rules, output and contact counting, regressions, progressions, and a prohibition on jumping down during reset prescriptions.
Exercise selection and progression should match physical and psychosocial readiness, technical competence, supervision, and equipment scale.

Accessibility can be improved with a lower soft-surface platform, visible takeoff line, contrasting box edge, landing footprint marks, demonstrated step-down route, longer reset, or a vertical jump-to-stick regression without assigning an exercise skill level.
A countermovement jump and a static squat jump have different start mechanics and performance characteristics, so start condition must be explicit.

Box height and landing hold are usually delivery modifiers; a static start, arm restriction, seated start, approach, unilateral landing, external load, or prior drop changes the exercise sufficiently to require a controlled variant or separate definition.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

The direct candidates for {{canonicalName}} were discovered through visible YouTube search; current availability and embedding, exact movement match, full viewing, captions, instructional quality, safety, and approval remain separate review gates.

assessmentSummary.identity: A bilateral countermovement jump from the floor onto a stable box, using a natural arm swing, followed by a bilateral full-foot landing, controlled stand, step-down exit, and complete reset.
currentCardFindings: The brief description captures the floor-to-box sequence but omits start condition, arm use, landing hold, box-height rule, edge clearance, and explicit prohibition on jumping down.
The capacity profile conflicts with a low-volume maximal-power identity and should be removed or made conditional rather than primary.
Taxonomy, anatomy, multidimensional difficulty, load, fatigue, constraints, support, time, scaling, and measurement fields are empty.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: all reps clear the edge and land with the full foot at a repeatable depth without hesitation or output loss

coachCues: Land quiet with the whole foot

Stand tall, step down, and reset before the next jump
commonFaults: chasing box height with excessive hip tuck

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Use this as the stable baseline identity.
